title: US Federal Reserve Outlines Coordinated Payments Fraud Response
discussion_signal: The post relays Federal Reserve survey and payment-fraud figures: 21% of U.S. adults experienced fraud or scams in 2024, non-credit-card fraud produced $84 billion in losses, and $21 billion was recovered. It frames fraud as a household, bank, payment-system, and trust problem and notes a coordinated public-private response. The aggregate figures do not show which victims recovered or the time and administrative cost of recovery.
linked_research_question: Who carries the unrecovered loss and recovery work after fraud, and do stronger detection systems reduce consumer burden or mainly shift friction before payment?
limits: The post summarizes official figures and does not independently verify them
Aggregate recovered dollars do not identify victim-level recovery rates or timing
A coordinated response announcement does not establish improved consumer outcomes
